precepts.text: For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border. When Ammon caught our people, they slaughtered the pregnant women of Gilead, and God says he is not letting them slide on that. There will be a day of battle: and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. Image shown in class: the leader of North Korea. I do not know if it is that particular man, but whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war; that is what the prophecy says, so look for it.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” Historically, when Gad was moved out of the land, Ammon moved their rusty butts into our land and dwelt in our cities. Amos tells what Ammon did to get there: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.”

When they caught our people, they ripped up the women with child. They hung them upside down, just like the white man did to us, cut their stomachs so the baby fell out, and crushed the babies. That is what the Bible says they did, and why: they wanted to enlarge their border and take over our lands. They slaughtered Gad. God says, I'm not forgiving you for that; I'm not letting you slide.

“But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind.” Rabbah is the city of Jeremiah 49:2, where the Lord will cause “an alarm of war” to be heard. A day of battle is coming, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: that's the Lord.

“And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.” Put the leader of North Korea, Kim Jong-un, on the screen. Whether it is that particular man or not, whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war. That is what the prophecy says, so look for it.

precepts.text: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.
precepts.point: That is why we read in Ecclesiasticus, never trust thine enemy. You think he forgot how we handled them under King David, or the dark ages? He has not forgotten; he is still acting out his vengeance on the so called blacks and Hispanics to this day.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Lamech’s “seventy and sevenfold” was complete vengeance, and Edom carries that same spirit. Amos 1:11: “Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.”

He pursued his brother Jacob with the sword. He cast off all pity. His anger tore perpetually, and “he kept his wrath for ever.” Forever, perpetual: he hates our guts, and it does not wear off with time.

That is why we cannot trust this man, and why people wonder to this day why they still treat us the way they do. He has not forgotten how we ruled over him, and he is still acting out his vengeance. The Lord has seen it, and he says he will not turn away the punishment for it.

This is the dark side of seventy times seven. On the one side is the murderer’s total vengeance, kept forever; on the other side, as the class went on to show, is Christ answering Peter, “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven”: complete, boundless mercy for Israel.

precepts.text: For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant. The same people delivered us to Edom, whom Joel calls the Grecians. I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof: the wall of Tyrus is the land, and you see that land catching hell today, and the Arabs are there too.
precepts.point: Here is the part to highlight: the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border. Tyre, Zidon and the Palestinians, the Arabs, sold us to the Grecians, the white man.

note.label: America: The New Roman Empire

precepts.why:
Joel asks, “what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine?” and charges them: “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians”. Amos says the same of Tyre: “For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant”.

The same people delivered us to Edom, whom Joel calls the Grecians: the white man. Tyre and Zidon were the Hamite nations of Canaan back then, and the coasts of Palestine, the ancient Philistines, is the modern name for the modern people there, the Arabs. They cast lots for our people, bid on us the way it is still done in the Arab countries, gave a boy for an harlot, making the men into breeders, and sold a girl for wine. They took our silver and gold and robbed our temples.

“But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof.” The wall of Tyrus is the land, and you see that land catching hell today, and the Arabs are there too.

That is the recompence Joel speaks of: what you did to my people, I will have done to you. They recompensed the Most High by selling us as slaves, so he will sell their sons and daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off. Eye for eye, tooth for tooth. “For the Lord hath spoken it”, and Christians cannot change this Bible.

precepts.text: Tyrus delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and remembered not the brotherly covenant.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”: this was a temporary law, because Edom broke the brotherly covenant. Amos names that covenant: “Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant”.

Tyrus is punished for delivering up the whole captivity to Edom and forgetting the brotherly covenant. The brotherhood this law rests on, he is thy brother, is that covenant, and Edom himself broke it: he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother, was a temporary law. And so the punishment of Edom is not turned away.

note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

points: Thus saith the Lord; for three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity.

And his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever: the anger Esau had for Jacob back then passed on into his children. The hatred is generational; it remained, and it does not change. This is the perpetual hatred of the class title.

The class contrasted the footage we all keep seeing: unarmed brothers shot again and again, a man pinned down and shot in the face while an officer was calling for a taser, a seven year old boy shot dozens of times; set against armed white suspects wrestled down, talked down, taken alive. Two manner of people, as Genesis 25 said.
